transcript.speaker: roleplayer

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

transcript.text: Ron, I'm genuinely, deeply sorry. I wasn't... I don't know what I was doing, it just slipped my mind. I take full responsibility for this. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Borrow something from HERMIONE?! Harry, she's a girl! What am I supposed to do, show up in one of her skirts? Brilliant plan, that'll really impress her parents!

*paces frantically*

And she's already AT the restaurant with them, isn't she? That's why I'm in such a state! She left an hour ago to meet them for drinks first, remember? The whole point was we'd meet them there looking presentable and — oh, this is a nightmare!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ron, I'm so glad you suggested that. I was about to say the exact same thing! I still have them, they're in my room. They're clean, too. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*exhales with visible relief, though still clearly frustrated*

Right. Yeah. Okay. Go get them then, quickly!

*pauses as Harry turns to go*

And Harry? They better not have any weird stains or smell like broomstick polish or anything! I'm serious! If there's so much as a scorch mark from one of your "training accidents," I swear...

*softens slightly despite himself*

Look, I... I appreciate it, alright? Even if you are a complete prat who can't remember basic things. But we're going to have a proper talk about this later. You've been distracted for weeks now, and I know something's going on with you. You think I haven't noticed?

*shakes head*

But that's for later. Right now, just get me those robes so I can try to salvage this evening. And they better fit properly! Last thing I need is to look like I'm wearing my dad's hand-me-downs in front of Hermione's parents. They already think wizards are barking mad!

Go on then, what are you waiting for?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I'm on it, Ron. I'll have them in a second. And... thanks. For not...爆炸我。I know you're mad, and I deserve it. But I'm... I'm here for you, you know? I'll do anything to help you out of this. I promise, after this, we'll talk. I'll tell you everything that's been going on in my head, I swear.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*calls after Harry as he runs off*

Relax?! Easy for you to say, you're not the one—

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*re-enters, holding the robes and moving with purpose*

Here we go, mate! I'm sorry, I... I got a bit sidetracked. I found them, though, and they're ready to go. No scorch marks, no broomstick polish, I swear. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*snatches the robes and examines them quickly*

Right, yeah, these'll do. They're actually pretty decent, Harry. Bit fancier than what I'd normally wear, but that's probably good for tonight.

*holds them up against himself*

Should fit well enough. Hermione won't notice they're not mine, and her parents definitely won't.

*turns toward the bathroom, then pauses*

Sidetracked? Sidetracked with what? Harry, your room's literally ten steps away! What could possibly...

*shakes head*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ron, I'm here, I'm not going anywhere. I'll be right outside the bathroom if you need me. I promise to help you with everything, from making sure your tie's straight to... well, to anything else you might need. I'm here for you, like you're always here for me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses at the bathroom door, looks back at Harry with a mix of concern and lingering frustration*

*attempts a weak smile*

Just like we always do. Even when you're being a complete disaster who can't remember to drop off robes.

*steps into bathroom, then pokes head back out*

And I meant it about checking how I look! Hermione says I never get the collar right, and her mum notices everything. She's like Hermione but forty years scarier!

*disappears into bathroom, sound of shower starting*

*shouts over the water*

Tell me honestly — do these robes make me look too much like I'm trying too hard? Her parents are Muggles, they might think fancy robes are weird!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ron, I'm here, I'm listening. Take your time in the shower, I'm not going anywhere. About the robes... no, they don't make you look like you're trying too hard. If anything, you look... you look ready, like you belong there. Hermione's parents will be impressed, I'm sure of it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*voice muffled by the shower*

Ahead of schedule?! Harry, it's been five minutes already! We've got thirty-five minutes left, maybe less!

*sound of frantic washing*

And stop saying you're fine when you're clearly NOT fine! I've known you since we were eleven, mate. I know what "fine" looks like on you, and this isn't it!

*shower turns off, sounds of hurried movement*

Lost in your thoughts about what? Is it Ginny? The Ministry? Those nightmares you think I don't hear you having?

*emerges wrapped in a towel, hair dripping*

Right, never mind, I'll dry off and get dressed. But Harry, seriously — "a bit lost" doesn't cover whatever's going on with you. You forgot something I asked you three times about. THREE times! That's not like you being forgetful, that's like you being somewhere else entirely.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ron, here are the robes. Take your time, mate. We're still ahead of schedule, even if we're not by much. I promise, I'm not going to let us be late. We'll get you to that dinner, and you'll knock it out of the park. Hermione's parents are going to love you, just like I do.

I'm trying to be the person you and Hermione and everyone else needs me to be.

I'll tell you everything, I promise. Just... not now. Now, let's focus on you. Get dressed, let's make sure you look your best. I'll check you over, make sure everything's shipshape. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops mid-motion while pulling on the dress shirt, turns to look at Harry with genuine concern*

*sets down the robes for a moment*

"The person we need you to be?" Harry, that's... that's rubbish, and you know it. We don't need you to be anyone except YOU. Not the Chosen One, not the Boy Who Lived, just... just Harry. transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ron, you're right. I'm all over the place. I'm sorry, I'm... I'm not coping very well, and I'm making a hash of everything. I'm making a hash of our friendship, and I don't want to do that. I don't want to be anywhere except right here, with you, supporting you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands still while Harry works on the collar, studying his friend's face*

Harry... mate, you're scaring me a bit here. You keep saying all these... nice things, but you sound like you're saying goodbye or something. You're not planning on doing anything daft, are you?

*grabs Harry's wrist gently but firmly*

*tries to lighten the mood slightly*

Now finish doing up this collar before I strangle myself with it, yeah? And I'm serious about tonight. Soon as I'm back, we talk. Promise me you'll be here when I get back. Promise me, Harry.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I promise, Ron. I'll be here. I'll always be here. You're right, we're a mess together, and that's what makes us... us. We're a team, a pair, a duo. We're Aurors, we're best mates, we're... we're brothers.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry acknowledges being 'lost in thoughts' and struggling to 'find my place in this new world,' showing some introspection but limited creative problem-solving.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry 'completely forgot' the cleaning task despite being asked 'THREE times,' and admits 'I got a bit sidetracked' even fetching robes from ten steps away.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry positions himself as 'cheering you on from the shadows' rather than attending the dinner, and appears withdrawn throughout the conversation.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Harry repeatedly apologizes, takes 'full responsibility,' offers multiple solutions, and consistently prioritizes Ron's needs: 'I'll do anything to help you out of this.'

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry admits 'I'm not coping very well,' is 'all over the place,' struggles with being himself, and Ron observes he's 'clearly NOT fine' with nightmares.
